defaultMessage: A product name can lead to several HS branches. Use the conditions to narrow the candidates, then confirm the national code for your shipment.

ambiguousQueries.message: Check conversion into a bed, frame or principal material, upholstery and construction. These are candidate branches, not a classification from the product name.
Distinguish a bed frame, convertible seat, medical bed, mattress support and mattress. Different components may need separate assessment.
Check material and whether the article is of a kind used in offices. A multi-material desk requires its construction to be reviewed.
A table may be medical furniture, office furniture, kitchen or bedroom furniture, or other furniture. Identify function and materials first.
Check specialist use, swivel and height adjustment, conversion, materials and upholstery before choosing a seat branch.
Check mattress construction and material. Air and water mattresses are outside Chapter 94; a hybrid description is not sufficient.
Confirm whether the chair both swivels and has variable height adjustment. Office use alone does not settle the six-digit seat code.
These branches cover qualifying convertible seats and exclude garden seats and camping equipment. Confirm wood versus other construction.
Cover material does not identify the frame or exclude a convertible seat. These results are candidate branches only.
Identify the parent article and the part. General-use hardware and certain independently described components are excluded; a complete unassembled article is not automatically parts.
Check material and construction. A stone or glass top on a different base requires a composite-product assessment.
Identify material and whether the goods are complete furniture, an unassembled complete article or separate parts.
Cabinet classification depends on material and its intended furniture function. A kitchen cabinet, office cabinet and bedroom cabinet need different branches.
Check the frame material and whether the product is actually a bed frame, a mattress support or a specialised medical bed.

Check whether the stool both swivels and adjusts in height; otherwise assess bamboo, rattan, other materials, frame and upholstery. A fixed bamboo or rattan stool does not belong in the adjustable-swivel branch merely because it is a bar stool.

Identify bamboo, rattan, other materials, the frame and upholstery. Check the special swivel-and-variable-height branch only if both functions are present. A chair marketed for dining is not classified from room use alone.

These are candidate seat-part branches, separated by wood versus other materials. First exclude general-use hardware and independently classified components, and distinguish parts from a complete unassembled seat.

These are candidate parts of other furniture, separated by wood versus other materials. The article must be an identifiable furniture part; review exclusions for general-use hardware, separate glass or stone sheets/slabs, and complete unassembled goods.
This branch includes eligible parts of qualifying dental, barber or similar chairs. Confirm the parent chair meets heading 9402, and check exclusions or independent headings for the component.

This branch includes eligible parts of the other medical, surgical, dental or veterinary furniture covered by 9402. Confirm the parent article and whether the component is separately described elsewhere.

Medical or salon in a product name does not establish the parent heading. Determine whether the parent is a qualifying 9402 chair or other medical furniture, or an ordinary 9401 seat, then assess the part and exclusions.
Separate seats, tables or storage furniture and loose cushions. Natural rattan and PE rattan are different materials.

excludedOrOutOfScope.message: A replacement gas lift or cylinder needs its own classification assessment. It is not automatically a seat part because it is used in an office chair.
General-use hardware may be excluded from Chapter 94. Check the applicable hardware or mechanical heading and the actual product rather than selecting furniture parts by its end use.
Chapter 94 Note 1(a) excludes pneumatic or water mattresses, pillows and cushions. This furniture dataset does not classify them.
Chapter 94 Note 3(A) excludes separately presented glass or stone sheets and slabs from its furniture-parts provisions. A complete assembled table is a different classification question.
This dataset does not cover standalone mirrors. Chapter 94 Note 1(b) excludes floor-standing mirrors. Furniture incorporating a mirror needs a review of the whole article.
Luminaires and lighting fittings are outside this dataset. Consult heading 9405 and applicable exclusions, including the Chapter 85 distinction.
Luminaires and lighting fittings are outside this dataset. Consult heading 9405 and applicable exclusions, including the Chapter 85 distinction.
Prefabricated buildings are outside this dataset; consult heading 9406 and its chapter note.

Architectural doors are outside this furniture dataset. A cabinet, wardrobe or cupboard door can instead be an identifiable furniture part; search that complete product phrase and check its material and construction.
This dataset covers the furniture and bedding branches of headings 9401–9404. It does not provide a complete building-materials HS table.
